messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Unable to process .cwa files (.csv is working well)
parts:
Hi Claire and Andrea,

GGIRread has been updated this week with improved functionality for cwa files, so probably it is related. Yesterday I submitted a new GGIR version to CRAN that should be compatible. So, hopefully the problem resolves itself when the new release of GGIR is accepted and available and by updating both GGIRread and GGIR.

In the meantime, if you do not want to wait then please install previous version of GGIRread via:
packageurl <- "https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/GGIRread/GGIRread_0.2.8.tar.gz"
install.packages(packageurl, repos=NULL, type="source")
Thanks,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

Dear All,

I'm encountering some problems processing my .cwa files. The only outputs I get are: Meta , Meta/Basic, results, results/QC folders. But each of these folders are empty.

I am using the same script as I have used in my previous processing for .cwa files (was able to successfully process everything then). I also tried to rerun using previous .cwa files that I had successfully processed and now have this issue.

However, the script is working fine for processing .csv files..

Would you be able to advise accordingly? Thanks :)

Regards,
Claire

parts:
You may want to check that the directory specified by datadir is real, because the error message indicates that GGIR has trouble accessing the file. Also make sure there are no non-accelerometer files in your datadir directory.

Also, please start a new thread because your question is about csv files while Claire's question is about cwa files. It is confusing to have two discussions in the same thread.

Vincent

Dear Vincent, 

i am also facing a problem with processing cwa file from axivity AX6. 
 could you please guide where is the problem in the sceiprt? also, I got an error about the readAxivity function
library(GGIR)

cwa_filepath <- "/Bologna/AGT-IT/AX6_Actigrah_recordings/CWA/CWA-DATA.CWA"
datadir <- "/Bologna/AGT-IT/AX6_Actigrah_recordings/CWA"
outputdir <- "/Bologna/AGT-IT/AX6_Actigrah_recordings/output"
study_name <- "Axivity_A6"

if (!file.exists(cwa_filepath)) {
  stop(paste("File does not exist: ", cwa_filepath))
}

if (!file.access(cwa_filepath, mode = 4) == 0) {
  stop(paste("File is not readable: ", cwa_filepath))
}

if (!dir.exists(outputdir)) {
  dir.create(outputdir, recursive = TRUE)
}

if (!file.access(outputdir, mode = 2) == 0) {
  stop(paste("Directory is not writable: ", outputdir))
}

study_outputdir <- file.path(outputdir, study_name)
if (!dir.exists(study_outputdir)) {
  dir.create(study_outputdir)
}

# reading Cwa filepath
cwa_data <- readAxivity(filename = cwa_filepath)

if (is.null(cwa_data$data) || nrow(cwa_data$data) == 0) {
  stop("No valid data found in the .cwa file.")
}

cwa_data$data <- cwa_data$data[, c("time", "x", "y", "z")]
na_indices <- which(is.na(cwa_data$data))
print(na_indices)

# Convert Unix timestamps to POSIXct format
cwa_data$data$time <- as.POSIXct(cwa_data$data$time, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")

# Run GGIR analysis for parts 1 to 5 using the modified data directly
ggir_results <- list()  # Create an empty list to store results

for (part in 1:5) {
  ggir_results[[part]] <- GGIR(part,
                               datadir = datadir,
                               outputdir = outputdir,
                               studyname = study_name,
                               do.report = part %in% c(2, 5),
                               f0 = 1,
                               f1 = NULL,
                               random = TRUE,
                               samplingrate = 1,
                               data = cwa_data$data)  # Use the modified data directly
  cat(paste("GGIR part", part, "completed.\n"))
}

# Save the ggir_results object to a file
output_file <- file.path(outputdir, "ggir_results.rds")
saveRDS(ggir_results, output_file)

cat(paste("GGIR analysis results saved to", output_file, "\n"))
print(cwa_filepath)


Regards, 

Abdul Haleem

parts: Dear Abdul,

i am also facing a problem with processing cwa file from axivity AX6.
could you please guide where is the problem in the sceiprt? also, I got an error about the readAxivity function
library(GGIR)
Did you update GGIR to latest 2.10-1 version?

cwa_filepath <- "/Bologna/AGT-IT/AX6_Actigrah_recordings/CWA/CWA-DATA.CWA"
datadir <- "/Bologna/AGT-IT/AX6_Actigrah_recordings/CWA"
outputdir <- "/Bologna/AGT-IT/AX6_Actigrah_recordings/output"
study_name <- "Axivity_A6"

Extension .CWA with capitals indicates that you copied the data from the file without OMGUI. Do you have the same problem if you extract it via OMGUI software which produces .cwa (lower case) extension?

for (part in 1:5) {
ggir_results[[part]] <- GGIR(part,
datadir = datadir,
outputdir = outputdir,
studyname = study_name,
do.report = part %in% c(2, 5),
f0 = 1,
f1 = NULL,
random = TRUE,
samplingrate = 1,
data = cwa_data$data) # Use the modified data directly
cat(paste("GGIR part", part, "completed.\n"))
}
This is not how function GGIR is intended. You are using arguments that do not exist in GGIR and by specifying mode = 1:5 you will process all 5 parts.

# Save the ggir_results object to a file
output_file <- file.path(outputdir, "ggir_results.rds")
saveRDS(ggir_results, output_file)

Function GGIR does not save output to R workspace, it stores all its results to an output folder. See package vignette for additional info: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html. Alternatively we also offer training courses: https://www.accelting.com/ggir-training/

Best, Vincent
